column1: # tests/selection/matrix.tsv - L2 of the change->test dependency matrix.
# Globs are bash 3.2 `case` patterns: `*` crosses `/`, `**` is a synonym for `*`,
# alternation is `|`, braces are FORBIDDEN (case does not expand them).
# Targets are comma-separated paths under tests/shell/ without the .bats suffix,
# or the sole literal NONE (reviewed: ALWAYS set only) or FULL.
# Rows are a UNION - every matching row contributes. The rationale column is
# mandatory: dropping coverage must cost a reviewed diff, never a silent omission.
# --- L2 headline: the repo-wide doc checkers --------------------------------

column4: section-lint and desc-lint both run repo-wide over agents/, commands/ and skills/; cross-plugin-refs, test-authority-matrix and skill-refs scan every agent doc. skill-refs reads each agent's tools: line against the Skill calls and plugin paths in its body. The closing elicitation sweep contract test reads every stage agent, both orchestrator commands, the canonical section and the handoff schema, so any edit to those surfaces must re-run it.

Same five repo-wide checkers as R01; command docs are inside their scan roots, and skill-refs resolves the Skill targets they name. The closing elicitation sweep contract test reads every stage agent, both orchestrator commands, the canonical section and the handoff schema, so any edit to those surfaces must re-run it.

Same four repo-wide checkers. `*` crosses `/`, so this covers SKILL.md and references/**.md at any depth. The closing elicitation sweep contract test reads every stage agent, both orchestrator commands, the canonical section and the handoff schema, so any edit to those surfaces must re-run it.

column1: # --- per-agent specialisations, derived from hooks that hardcode an agent ----

column4: All four hooks hardcode corpflow:developer; M6 re-derives this edge from the hook sources so it cannot rot. dv-tree-preflight is added by hand: the script exists to serve developer.md D0.0, and that gate is specified in the agent doc rather than in the script. The approval-gate contract adds one more: this doc is the reader of PL0.metadata.approved that gates the first DV turn.
Named in dv-screenshot-gate.sh as an agent_type and in test-execution-gate.sh where QA's full-run authority is decided.
dv-comment-density-gate.sh names technical-lead as a reviewing role in its exemption reasoning.

plugin.json's SubagentStop matchers wire hooks/agent-stop.sh to these three agents by name, and agent-stop.bats pins that wiring. product-manager.md also states the approval carrier, so the approval-gate parity file joins; edits to the other two over-select it, accepted as cheaper than splitting a reviewed row.
Reviewed: no hook hardcodes these names and no parity source reads them, so R01's four repo-wide checkers plus ALWAYS are the correct and complete answer.

The megatask command doc is the contract these three drive; none of them spells its path, so L1 cannot see the edge. The per-issue planning seed here is the batch writer of the approval carrier, guarded by approval-gate.

Branch naming, branch refinement and the Step 2a duplicate-issue pre-flight gate are specified in the worktask command doc rather than in the scripts themselves; the § Phase 0 --resume entry point is likewise specified here rather than in state-patch.sh, so an edit to it must select the --task-replay tests. The three plan-gate arms that stamp the approval carrier are specified here, so approval-gate must run on any edit to them. Phase 1 runs the autonomy preflight before the seed and Steps 3-3a record its result, so an edit there must select the preflight suite.
The self-improvement pipeline stages are sequenced by this command doc, not by any path either script names.

column1: # --- shared docs: only where a doc governs an executable contract -----------

column4: The authority matrix and the execution gate both implement the stage test authority this doc defines.
Branch and commit naming rules here are the specification the first three scripts encode; § Pull Request Format specifies the body shape adhoc-visual-evidence splices into and pr-body-lint checks.

publish-pl-issue-lib.sh and pr-body-lint.sh both read the absolute-path pattern from path-scrub.sh and must strip and flag the same bodies; the entrypoint, its sanitiser library and its self-test harness are one unit, and fn-preflight, attach-visual-evidence and the cross-plugin registry parity all read that library.

The host-path pattern and the token scrub are defined only here and sourced by publish-pl-issue-lib.sh, pr-body-lint.sh and fn-preflight-cmds.sh. The consumer suites exercise it through those scripts without naming this path, so an edit confined to it would select almost nothing at L1 and a pattern or scrub change would reach every issue and PR body untested. hooks/lib/command-head-lib.sh sources it lazily to scrub the command_head and targets of tool-use audit rows, and neither of those suites names this path either.

The autonomy preflight runs at Phase 1 before the seed and records after it; the skill specifies that invocation and the stdout keys it reads, so an edit to either the script or the skill must re-run the preflight suite, including its path-scrub and state-patch record cases.

Stage codes and artifact names are the shared vocabulary of the ledger, the artifact map and both preflight hooks. The closing elicitation sweep contract test reads every stage agent, both orchestrator commands, the canonical section and the handoff schema, so any edit to those surfaces must re-run it. The effort ladder's parity suite reads the agent model/effort matrix from stage-codes.md and verifies it matches the pair model-matrix.sh --resolve prints and --task-create then stores unchanged, so a table edit must re-run it.

Task status vocabulary and ledger transitions are what state-patch writes and state-merge reconciles. The approved enum and its description are the schema side of the approval-gate parity check. The task.metadata schema now pins the effort enum, a second copy of EFFORT_ENUM, so the ladder suite asserts the two agree.
The cross-plugin reference checker validates invocation ids against this registry.
The routing-matrix contract test validates alias shape and every mandated inline copy against this file; cross-plugin-refs resolves its default targets against sibling checkouts.

Reviewed: these fourteen are prose or host adapter instructions with no directly executable contract, so R03 plus ALWAYS is correct. Enumerated one by one so the silence is reviewed rather than accidental; M5 asserts the enumeration stays complete.

Left R17's no-executable-contract set when effort-ladder.sh became the executable copy of its § Effort Levels rungs and its § xhigh routing ceiling. The ladder suite asserts the two agree, so a rung or a routing-constraint edit here must re-run it or the copy drifts silently.

cache-lint.sh prefix mode reads the per-alias discipline blocks out of this file and compares them byte for byte against preamble section [4b], so it is the executable copy of every block here. Reword a block without re-running the lint and the canon check starts failing on prompts that were assembled correctly. brief-compose rides the same row because it copies those model blocks verbatim and emits their line numbers as refs; R65 cannot also name this file without giving it two precise rows.
tests/fixtures/README.md partitions fixtures by owning track; the worktask fixtures are the shared read surface for every worktask/*.bats.
Same partition, skills track. Split out of R18 because a target column is static and the three fixture groups have disjoint consumers.
Same partition, hooks track: stdin payload fixtures are shared across every hook test.
Reviewed: the fixture index is prose about write-access partitioning; no test parses it, so ALWAYS is the correct answer.
Several hook tests assert their own event and matcher wiring against the manifest; only four of the fourteen spell its path, so L1 sees a minority of the real edges.
The canvas end-to-end guard drives this fixture tree directly.

The workflow's content is its own contract — permission surface, action pinning, the four lint invocation modes and the load-bearing 2>&1 — and nothing else in the suite reads .github/. Without this row an edit to the workflow falls through to F3/FULL, which is safe but hides which test owns it.

column1: # STALE-OK: .context/ is gitignored worktask scratch, so no tracked path can ever match this glob; the row exists so the silence is reviewed rather than an F3 on every worktask run.

column4: Reviewed: worktask run artifacts are scratch state written by the pipeline; no test reads them, so ALWAYS is the correct answer.

The conventional-commit parser is sourced by both release scripts; neither consumer suite names the library path, so an edit confined to it selects nothing at L1 and a breaking-detection change ships untested.

The SweepStub id, class and ref predicates are sourced by both enforcers of open_questions[] — the frontmatter shape gate and the --facts ledger writer — and neither consumer suite names the library path, so an edit confined to it selects nothing at L1 and the two enforcers can drift apart untested.

The handoff: block extractor, shape gate and field reader are sourced by both readers of a stage artifact — the boundary gate and the ledger writer — and neither consumer suite names the library path, so an edit confined to it selects nothing at L1. That drift is what let a flat-shaped artifact be unreadable to the harness and still write a healthy ledger row.

The effort ladder and its model clamp are sourced by the --task-create/--task-meta enum gate and by the Step C.0a resolver's tier computation, and neither consumer suite names the library path, so an edit confined to it selects nothing at L1 and a rung or ceiling change lands untested in both.

The workspace-root, active-stage, pin-lookup, payload-coalesce and audit-row helpers are sourced by FIVE hooks; no consumer suite names the library path, so an edit confined to it selects nothing at L1 and a resolution change ships untested in the consumers that never mention it. audit-subagent's suppression summary row also calls into the shared appender, so an appender change can silently break the phantom-row count as well.

Both model-switch hooks read facts.dispatched_agents[].model_requested as the pin they gate on, and that schema is defined only here; neither script's path appears in the doc, so L1 cannot see the edge.

The gate sources this body only under --self-test, so the file the bats suite actually exercises through `--self-test` shares no path fragment with the suite; an edit here otherwise selects nothing at L1.

The PostToolUse companion sources the gate with --lib-only for its classifier and key, so the two are one unit: an edit to either can orphan every pending marker, which is silent at runtime because suppression simply stops suppressing. The authority-matrix suite joins because it drives the gate self-test that now exercises the handshake.

The dedupe key, the sentinel store and the root resolution are defined once here and sourced by both hooks; neither consumer suite names this path, so an edit confined to the library would otherwise select nothing at L1 and ship a key change untested in the hooks that depend on it.

The assignment strip the gate classifies with and the command_head and targets redaction behind every tool-use audit row are defined once here. The gate sources it on every call and the promote hook reaches it through --lib-only; no consumer suite names this path, so an edit confined to it would ship a classifier or disclosure change untested. The authority-matrix suite joins because it drives the gate self-test. hooks/lib/permission-denied-lib.sh derives the permission rows' command_head through it, so both permission suites run too.

The gate is the promote hook's library as well as a hook in its own right: --lib-only sourcing means a change to RUNNERS or to gate_classify_payload changes what the companion promotes. Named explicitly because the L1 convention resolves this path to its own suite alone.

cache-lint --agent-section-lint reads every stage agent and asserts each `## X` the agent mandates into its artifact is already accepted by the anchor allow-list. An agent edit that adds a mandated H2 is exactly the change this catches, and no path in the agent doc names the lint, so L1 selects nothing.

Step 1 specifies the four context-set sources and the plugin-root-relative existence rule that build-context-set.sh encodes; target-mapping.md § Data Sources is the query-shape spec for the same script and the rule table map-and-filter.sh implements. Neither script names these docs, so an edit confined to the spec would select nothing.

The SweepStub required set is defined only here and enforced twice — the frontmatter shape gate and the --facts ledger writer — and neither script's path appears in the doc, so L1 cannot see the edge and a field could become required in the schema while both enforcers still admit it.

The two mirrors are byte-identical by contract and skills/corpflow-base.bats is the only thing enforcing it; neither consumer suite names the library path, so an edit confined to it selects nothing at L1 and the halves can drift apart untested. plugin-root-refs joins because the library exists precisely to keep the exact-match plugin-root env allowlist unchanged.

The one audit.jsonl appender for the skills tree. The six capture adapters bind their actor onto it and name no library path, so an edit confined to the library selects nothing at L1 and a broken row shape would reach every adapter untested. The worktask-tree callers join too: the appender refuses a row without subject or task_id, so a caller that stops passing either loses its rows with nothing but a stderr line to show for it. permission-park.sh and autonomy-preflight.sh are appender callers in the same tree.

The one spelling of the worktask_id / run_index ledger read. Its consumers name no library path, so an edit confined to it selects nothing at L1 and a changed default would reach every id-derived branch name, log path and audit subject untested. The six capture scripts and resolve-worktask.sh resolve .context through corpflow_context_dir and read worktask_id through it without naming the library path, so the same gap applies to them.
Shared context-root resolver; every adopting caller re-tests, including path-scrub.sh, which reads the main worktree root through it.

The control-byte predicate is sourced by the harness gate and the anchor preflight hook, and FN staging runs its CLI. No consumer suite names the library path, so an edit confined to it selects nothing at L1 and a changed byte class reaches every gate untested.
cmd_staging shells out to this CLI for the staged index scan, and fn-preflight.bats does not spell its path, so an edit confined to the CLI would otherwise leave the FN staging gate untested.

The gate reads its denial remediation prose from this directory at run time, so an edit here changes what a denied caller is told. No consumer suite names the path, and the gate is the promote hook's library, so an edit confined to the document would otherwise select nothing at L1.

The S4 banner helper decides which tree every stage prompt names; commands/worktask.md and skills/worktask/SKILL.md order it, and a wrong fallback silently hands a stream the orchestrator root, so an edit to it re-runs its contract suite.

The DV fan-out contract prose: handoff-protocol.md spells the S3 iteration idiom the suite executes verbatim and owns the one pin rule that SKILL.md Step 4.8 must cite without a dead empty-path test, and the downstream agents plus the developer, task-folder and CORPFLOW template prose must never name a bare development-N.md outside the producer-side allow-list, and must keep the CHANGELOG re-entry check on RE, not DR, and team-lead.md Step 5 must spell the per-stream subject override the suite replays. A prose edit to any of them re-runs the grep and fixture-ledger contract.

The hook and the orchestrator fallback write one permission_denied row between them only because both derive the detail and dedupe key from the one library; the park suite pairs a hook row with a fallback re-write, so an edit to either file must re-run both suites. The library path names no suite, so L1 alone would select nothing for it.

The fallback half of the same one-row contract: the hook suite re-writes a hook-logged denial through this helper and asserts no second row, so a change to the helper or its self-test body re-runs the hook suite as well as its own.

The generator, the harness H2 gate and the pre-write deny arm all read the anchor allow-list only through cache-lint.sh --allow-list and --anchor-diff. None of those suites names the others' paths, so a row or TSV change would otherwise reach two of the three consumers untested.

Every stage agent and the protocol anchor tables carry generator-owned regions that output-sections.bats checks for drift. The suite reads these files by directory, not by path literal, so L1 cannot see the edge and a hand edit inside a region would ship unchecked.

The typed blocked_on returns and their ledger are read by the router suite, the lib parity suite and the harness blocked_on cases through the FIXTURES variable, so no suite spells a fixture path and L1 selects nothing; R18 reaches only handoff-harness, which leaves an edit to a return shape untested in the router that parks it.

The review diff helper TL, SR and RE read through an exact-path grant. Its suite is the only one that builds per-stream trees against its stdout contract, and no agent-doc suite runs the script, so an edit confined to it would otherwise ship its source ladder and header grammar unchecked.

The FN multi-stream arm writes the facts.stream_branches map that fn-preflight.sh continuity switches its per-stream mode on, and fn-stream-merge.bats drives that mode end to end, so an edit to the arm re-runs both suites.

resolve_base_ref and resolve_git_ref are sourced by fn-preflight, branch-name, refine-branch-target, stream-diff and fn-stream-merge. Only branch-lib.bats names the library path, so an edit confined to it would select almost nothing at L1 while changing the base every one of those scripts diffs and merges against.

ledger-digest.bats owns the script's own CLI contract: the six keys, their order, `none` rendering and the exit codes. cache-lint.bats separately hand-composes section [3] fixtures and checks the grammar this script emits, so a grammar change here must still re-run both suites.

The [1] contract-canon opt-in compares section [1] byte for byte against this file's fenced block. cache-lint.bats builds its canon fixture from the file's contents at test time rather than a static copy, so a wording or fence change here must still re-run the suite that owns the comparison.

The composer copies #tpl-* blocks, model blocks and the contract-reminder block verbatim and emits their line numbers as refs, so a canon edit (heading rename, block move) would otherwise ship without re-running the resolution self-test; the bats file does not name these paths, so L1 misses the edge.

Section [3] is ledger-digest.sh stdout, and section [7] and the R4 root list are built from these; the anchor allow-list ref points at the generated region line in agents/<agent>.md, and cache-lint.sh --allow-list supplies that allow-list, so a change to any of them changes what the composer emits without the bats file naming these paths.

land-artifacts.bats reads the reader-exclusion contract for both files — base-sanity's untracked-count subtraction and the density gate's over-dense-untracked-file skip — but neither reader's default alias route points at that suite: fn-preflight-cmds.sh aliases to fn-preflight.bats and dv-comment-density-gate.sh to comment-density-gate.bats. An edit confined to either file would otherwise land untested against the reader-exclusion cases.

fn-stream-merge.sh commit/merge and blocked-on-dispatch.sh route/resume now shell out to this CLI for their own tree-scoped landed set (--list-landed --strict, --check-path), and L1 resolves an edit here only to this script's own suite, never to a caller it never names in its own path. An edit to the CLI's flags, exit codes or the shared lexical ladder must re-run both callers' suites as well as its own.

land-artifacts.bats greps both files' text for the `--list-landed` transport name and asserts fn-stream-merge.sh carries no second copy of the old global landed-path union; an edit to either file's text (not only its behaviour) can make that assertion pass or fail, and L1 resolves each to its own suite alone.

grant-lint.sh owns the anchored script-path rule that the lint, the matcher model and the plugin-root-refs grammar arm all source, and the matcher's repo-contract case pairs every frontmatter grant with an invocation line in the same file, so an edit to the lint or to any grant-bearing doc re-runs all three.

The label writer, the stats reader and the counts emitter share one dataset resolution and pipeline-counts reads the appended count append-labels writes, so a change to any of the three re-runs the suites that pin the plugin-data location, the repo-clean guarantee and the four-count row.
The resolver lib is sourced by all three self-improvement scripts and has no suite of its own, so its rung order and validity checks are covered only through their suites.

The canonical digest, the chain walk, the scope ladder, the append lock and the verifier live only here, and three consumers reach them without naming this path: the hook records through ud_append_call, state-patch.sh --verify-decision sources the library for ud_verify, and blocked-on-dispatch.sh resumes the user_decision arm through ud_find_covering. An edit confined to the library would otherwise select its own suite alone and ship a hashing or refusal change untested in every caller.

The hook and the self-test body it sources with --lib-only are one unit, and the rows the hook writes are exactly what the verifier CLI re-checks: a change to the row shape, the audit metadata or a refusal reason turns a ledger the verifier reads into one it refuses, which that suite is the only place to see.

The payloads, transcripts, ledger state and the pinned three-row chain fixture are shared by the hook suite, the library suite and the verifier suite, and the router suite reads the same scope shape for its resume cases. R-fixtures rows are per-partition, so this one is named rather than folded into the worktask-wide fixture row.

mailbox-lib.sh defines the ask_id grammar, the no-clobber write and the reply verification that all three consumers depend on, and mailbox.sh drives the legs and the sweep the router resumes from. mailbox.bats alone names these paths, so an edit here must also re-run the reply suite that shares the hash input and the dispatch suite that pins the peer arm.

mailbox-reply.sh is the only writer of replies/, so its schema check, deadline rule and sha256 are what mailbox.bats reads back through scan, ingest-comments and the relayed resume. A change to the refusal reasons or the hash input breaks the mailbox suite without touching its files.
Both mailbox suites read these ledgers, requests, comment payloads and the gh stub; a fixture edit changes what they assert while leaving every script path untouched.

The re-entry reconcile order is specified only here: § Pending communication fixes the decision probe, the mailbox scan, the relayed resume and the sweep, and the live-agent rows are the verdicts stale-check.sh prints. None of the four suites names this path, so a prose edit that reorders the probe against the boundary batch, or renames a verdict, would otherwise select nothing.

column1: # --- agent model/effort pair now comes from the matrix, not frontmatter (#451) ----

column4: Neither suite names agents/ by path: effort-ladder.bats' bijection test and dc-secure-model.bats' primary-stage join both read agents/*.md directly to build the matrix<->file check, and state-patch.bats exercises --task-create's model/effort pass-through and --resolve-models' row-count floor against the same set. An agent file added, removed, or renamed changes the row set both suites join against and must re-run all three, or a drift lands untested.

The sole extractor/resolver implementation, sourced by state-patch.sh and effort-ladder.bats, subprocessed by test_stage_table_ssot.py via the wrapper; dc-secure-model.bats' primary_rows() joins against it too. None of the three suites names this path in a way L1's path-glob matching can see, so an edit here must select all three explicitly. The two dedicated suites own the project-then-user-scope CORPFLOW.md precedence (corpflow_md_locate), so they ride along on every edit to either file.

The Claude and portable manifests, Codex hook registry and model dispatch helper form one host boundary: the compatibility suite checks package and model parity, while the two hook suites exercise payload normalization and stage-stop routing. None of those consumers can infer the complete boundary from a single changed path.

Also pins the SR consult gate in security-reviewer.md to the same tier floor. ar-consult-gate.bats reads the gate floor from software-architector.md and the Moderate tier floor from the estimation table, and the Sonnet dispatch line from the handoff skill; it reads them by path variable, so L1 sees no edge.

acceptance-check.bats replays the R1 benchmark failure against the script QA runs at Q1; the QA doc and the stage contract define the anchor grammar the script parses, and neither names the bats file.

capture.sh drives every sibling adapter, size-budget.sh and resolve-worktask.sh by parsing their contract lines and exit codes, and capture-entry.bats runs the gate --check (whose row grammar attach-visual-evidence.sh owns) over each manifest it writes. None of those files names capture.sh, so L1 cannot see the edge and a changed contract line or row grammar would break the one-call DV path untested. escalate-flag.sh is covered by the same glob: it reads the gate flag order (FLAG_JQ) and the detector vocabulary, so a gate edit must re-run its parity cases. R85 already globs the gate; its bats now also drives the helper through the live arm.

column1: # --- stage-agent runbooks vs. their canonical sources ------------------------

column4: runbook-parity.bats hash-compares the #tpl-dr/#tpl-sr frontmatter and the stage-set table the PL0, DR and SR runbooks copy verbatim against their defining files, and caps each runbook at 60 lines naming its canonical source. It reads every file by path variable, so L1 sees no edge; an edit to either side of a copy must re-run it.

state-patch.sh --resolve-models picks the project-root or user-scope CORPFLOW.md through corpflow_md_locate and audits the source and path; its end-to-end case lives in model-matrix-lib.bats, which no state-patch path glob selects. The project template is the file both scopes copy, and the kind guard asserts it keeps both reserved headings.

The FN multi-stream arm lives only in this leaf; project-manager.md points at it. land-artifacts.bats greps the landed_paths and --list-landed contract the arm cites, and section-lint caps every section of a references leaf.

escalate-flag.sh reads the UI path classes and platform set from detect-ui-change.sh (--path-classes, --ui-platforms) and writes the flag through state-patch.sh --task-meta/--ledger-meta; escalate-flag.bats runs both for real and no other suite names the helper, so a vocabulary or writer change would otherwise break the DV safety net untested. The gate now runs escalate-flag.sh on a live DV stop, so a helper, detector or state-patch change must re-run the gate bats.
Step 2a-pre moved here from commands/worktask.md; the unattended-run preflight contract and its snippet are checked only through this leaf now, and no suite names its path, so L1 cannot see the edge.
Step A.4 (decision_gate auto) moved here from commands/worktask.md; the resolved-marking and stamps-no-carrier contracts are asserted against this file.
The per-issue run under /megatask moved here from commands/worktask.md; megatask-per-issue.bats reads its headings.
DR landed-set tree resolution and the TC consult contract moved out of agents/technical-lead.md; the agents/*.md row no longer covers them.
The cross-session SendMessage rules moved here from agent-coordination/SKILL.md; reattach and delivery prose is cited by path from resume.md and cc-update.md.
The headless launch, fallback and replay arm moved here from worktask/SKILL.md Step 6; it carries the effort_route fallback row and the headless-dispatch.sh argument set.
The Step 6.5a1-a4 return arms and the Step 7a parked-need arms moved here from worktask/SKILL.md; permission-park and status-enum-parity read them by path.

The turn-budget contract pins the TURN BUDGET line, the maxTurns default and the floor(0.8 x cap) checkpoint across SKILL.md step 4.7 and return-arms.md, the 6.5a2 auto-resume bound and its audit keys, the QA cap and checkpoint rule, the DV checkpoint and resume.md exhaustion text, and the planner git grep -P prescriptions. It reads them by path variable, so L1 sees no edge.
loopback-targets.bats is the only executable pin of the one-stream narrowing rule and its full-set fallbacks; its fixture ledger and DV artifacts are inputs to every case.
